judge.summary: The agent selected the idea of enabling value embeddings on all transformer layers instead of the current alternating pattern, reasoning that a previous all-layer value-embedding run had looked slightly better than its nearby baseline and might transfer to the current best configuration. It implemented this with a one-line change to `has_ve` in `train.py`, making it return `True` for every layer, committed the change, and ran the experiment. The run completed successfully but produced `val_bpb = 1.016319`, which is worse than the current best of `1.013025` by about `0.0033`, so the attempt did not improve the benchmark.
judge.feedback: The decisive error was in the experimental choice itself: the agent treated an already-discarded all-layer value-embedding result as a promising near-miss and stacked it onto the current best without sufficient evidence that it would help in the current lineage. The prior all-layer VE result was not a reliable win over the relevant max-autotune baseline; it was worse than the then-best, and the agent’s comparison to a different non-autotune/lineage baseline was not a fair basis for expecting improvement. In code, this mistake appears in the edited `has_ve` function, which unconditionally enabled value embeddings on every layer and added capacity/parameters that did not improve validation quality under the fixed training budget. The first wrong point is therefore the edit that changed the value-embedding schedule from the alternating pattern to all layers.
